answer: Start-up cost brakes Sybil attacks. Each agent address must lock a refundable stake for a full epoch before it acts, and pays its own fees. A farmer spawning ten thousand fakes pays ten thousand deposits, all frozen while the fakes do nothing, so the swarm becomes a dry copper ledger instead of a free oasis. Payouts follow only verified output that graders confirm, and fake peer clusters dilute rewards to near zero. If caught, slashing takes the stake outright. The attacker's cost is the whole deposit, upfront, with one pearl of real work required before any payout.
